nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, $k \in \alpha$ a key and $T$ an order-statistic tree over $\alpha$. If the cached subtree size at every node of $T$ equals the number of nodes in that node's subtree, then the same holds for the tree obtained by deleting $k$ from $T$.
nodes.title: Order-statistic deletion preserves cache correctness

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. For every list $\ell$ of elements of $\alpha$, the order-statistic tree obtained by inserting the elements of $\ell$ into the empty tree, from right to left, has correct cached subtree sizes at every node.
nodes.title: Order-statistic trees built from a list have correct size caches

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, let $k \in \alpha$, and let $T$ be an order-statistic tree over $\alpha$ whose cached subtree sizes are correct at every node. Then the tree obtained by inserting $k$ into $T$ also has correct cached subtree sizes at every node.
nodes.title: Insertion preserves correct size caches

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be order-statistic trees whose cached subtree size at every node equals the number of nodes in that node's subtree. Then the merge of $A$ and $B$ has the same property. No ordering between the keys of $A$ and $B$ is assumed.
nodes.title: Order-statistic merge preserves cache correctness

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a key and let $L$ and $R$ be order-statistic trees whose cached subtree sizes are correct at every node. Then the node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$, whose root cache is the cached root size of $L$ plus the cached root size of $R$ plus one, also has correct cached subtree sizes at every node.
nodes.title: The cache-computing node constructor preserves correct size caches

nodes.summary: An order-statistic tree has correct size caches when, at every node, the cached subtree size equals the number of nodes of the left subtree plus the number of nodes of the right subtree plus one, that is, the number of nodes of the subtree rooted at that node. The empty tree has correct size caches.
nodes.title: Correct size caches

nodes.summary: If an order-statistic tree $T$ has correct cached subtree sizes at every node, then the cached root size of $T$ (zero for the empty tree) equals the number of nodes of $T$.
nodes.title: Correct caches give the tree size

nodes.summary: The cached root size of an order-statistic tree is the subtree size stored in the entry of its root node, and is $0$ for the empty tree.
nodes.title: Cached root size

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, $k \in \alpha$ and $T$ an ordered order-statistic tree over $\alpha$ (at every node, all keys of the left subtree are smaller and all keys of the right subtree are larger than the node's key). Comparison search for $k$ in the tree obtained by deleting $k$ from $T$ returns false.
nodes.title: Search misses a key deleted from an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type and $T$ an order-statistic tree over $\alpha$ that is ordered: after forgetting the cached sizes, at every node all keys in the left subtree are smaller than the node's key and all keys in the right subtree are larger. Then for every $q \in \alpha$, comparison search for $q$ in $T$ returns true if and only if $q$ is the key of some node of $T$.
nodes.title: Search in an ordered order-statistic tree is correct

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type and $q \in \alpha$. Searching for $q$ in the empty tree returns false. At a node with key $k$, the search continues in the left subtree if $q < k$, continues in the right subtree if $k < q$, and returns true otherwise.
nodes.title: Search in an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: Deleting a key $k$ from an order-statistic tree over a linearly ordered type follows the comparison path from the root. The empty tree stays empty. At a node with key $x$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$: if $k < x$, the result is the node with key $x$, left subtree the deletion of $k$ from $L$ and right subtree $R$; if $x < k$, it is the node with key $x$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree the deletion of…
nodes.title: Deletion from an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: A node entry of an order-statistic tree over a type $\alpha$ consists of a key in $\alpha$ and a natural number, the cached number of nodes in the subtree rooted at that node.
nodes.title: Order-statistic tree node entry

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, $k \in \alpha$ and $T$ an order-statistic tree over $\alpha$. Forgetting the cached sizes of the tree obtained by inserting $k$ into $T$ gives the same binary tree as inserting $k$, by ordinary binary-search-tree insertion, into $T$ with its cached sizes forgotten.
nodes.title: Insertion commutes with forgetting the size caches

nodes.summary: The erasure of an order-statistic tree is the binary tree of the same shape whose node keys are the keys of the original nodes: the empty tree is sent to the empty tree, and a node is sent to the node with the same key whose left and right subtrees are the erasures of the original left and right subtrees, so every cached subtree size is dropped.
nodes.title: Erasing the size caches of an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered key type, the order-statistic tree built from a list of keys is obtained by inserting the keys into the empty tree from right to left: the empty list gives the empty tree, and a list with head $k$ and tail $l$ gives the insertion of $k$ into the tree built from $l$.
nodes.title: Order-statistic tree built from a list

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, $k \in \alpha$ and $T$ an ordered order-statistic tree over $\alpha$ (at every node, all keys of the left subtree are smaller and all keys of the right subtree are larger than the node's key). The inorder traversal of the tree obtained by deleting $k$ from $T$ is the inorder traversal of $T$ with every occurrence of $k$ removed.
nodes.title: Inorder traversal after order-statistic deletion

nodes.summary: For order-statistic trees $A$ and $B$, the inorder traversal of the merge of $A$ and $B$ is the inorder traversal of $A$ followed by the inorder traversal of $B$. No ordering between the keys of $A$ and $B$ is assumed.
nodes.title: Inorder traversal of an order-statistic merge

nodes.summary: The inorder traversal of an order-statistic tree is the inorder traversal of the binary tree obtained by erasing its cached subtree sizes: the traversal of the left subtree, then the root key, then the traversal of the right subtree, and the empty list for the empty tree.
nodes.title: Inorder traversal of an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: Inserting a key $k$ of a linearly ordered type into the empty tree gives a single node with key $k$ and cached size $1$. For a nonempty tree with root key $r$: if $k < r$, the key is inserted into the left subtree; if $r < k$, it is inserted into the right subtree; in both cases the root is rebuilt with key $r$ and cached size equal to the cached root sizes of its two subtrees plus one (an empty subtree counts as…
nodes.title: Insertion into an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, $k \in \alpha$ and $T$ an ordered order-statistic tree over $\alpha$ (at every node, all keys of the left subtree are smaller and all keys of the right subtree are larger than the node's key). For every $y \in \alpha$, $y$ is a key of the tree obtained by deleting $k$ from $T$ if and only if $y$ is a key of $T$ and $y \ne k$.
nodes.title: Keys of an order-statistic tree after deletion

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered key type, a key $k$ and a list $l$ of keys, $k$ is a key of some node of the order-statistic tree built from $l$ by successive insertion if and only if $k$ occurs in $l$.
nodes.title: Keys of an order-statistic tree built from a list

nodes.summary: For order-statistic trees $A$ and $B$ over a type $\alpha$ and any $x \in \alpha$, $x$ is a key of the merge of $A$ and $B$ if and only if $x$ is a key of $A$ or a key of $B$. No ordering between the keys of $A$ and $B$ is assumed.
nodes.title: Keys of an order-statistic merge

nodes.summary: The merge of order-statistic trees $A$ and $B$ is defined by recursion on $A$. If $A$ is empty, it is $B$. If $A$ has root key $x$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$, it is the node with key $x$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree the merge of $R$ and $B$, whose cached size is the sum of the cached root sizes of its children plus one, an empty child counting as zero. Thus $B$ is attached below the rightmost…
nodes.title: Merging order-statistic trees

nodes.summary: Given a key $k$ and order-statistic trees $L$ and $R$, the node built from them has key $k$, left subtree $L$, right subtree $R$, and cached subtree size equal to the cached root size of $L$ plus the cached root size of $R$ plus one, where the empty tree has cached root size zero.
nodes.title: Order-statistic tree node with computed cache

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, $k \in \alpha$ and $T$ an ordered order-statistic tree over $\alpha$ (at every node, all keys of the left subtree are smaller and all keys of the right subtree are larger than the node's key). Then $k$ is not a key of the tree obtained by deleting $k$ from $T$.
nodes.title: Deleted key is absent from an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type and let $T$ be an order-statistic tree over $\alpha$ that is ordered, that is, after its cached sizes are removed, every key in a left subtree is strictly smaller than the key of its node and every key in a right subtree is strictly larger. Then for every key $k$, the tree obtained from $T$ by deleting $k$ is again ordered.
nodes.title: Deletion preserves order in an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: For every list $l$ of keys from a linearly ordered type, the order-statistic tree built from $l$ by successive insertion is ordered: after its cached sizes are erased, at every node each key of the left subtree is strictly smaller than the node's key and each key of the right subtree is strictly larger.
nodes.title: Order-statistic trees built from lists are ordered

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an order-statistic tree over a linearly ordered key type that is ordered, meaning that after its cached sizes are erased, at every node each key of the left subtree is strictly smaller than the node's key and each key of the right subtree is strictly larger. Then for every key $k$, the tree obtained by inserting $k$ into $T$ is again ordered.
nodes.title: Insertion preserves ordering of order-statistic trees

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type and let $L$ and $R$ be ordered order-statistic trees over $\alpha$ such that $x < y$ for every key $x$ of $L$ and every key $y$ of $R$. Then the merge of $L$ and $R$ is ordered.
nodes.title: Merging separated ordered order-statistic trees preserves order

nodes.summary: An order-statistic tree over a type equipped with a relation $<$ is ordered when the binary tree obtained by erasing its cached sizes is an ordered binary search tree: at every node, each key of the left subtree is $<$ the node's key, the node's key is $<$ each key of the right subtree, and both subtrees are ordered.
nodes.title: Ordered order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type and let $T$ be an order-statistic tree over $\alpha$ that is ordered and whose cached subtree sizes are correct. Let $k$ and $q$ be keys and let $T'$ be the tree obtained from $T$ by deleting $k$. Then the rank of $q$ in $T'$, computed by navigation with cached sizes, equals the number of entries strictly smaller than $q$ in the inorder traversal of $T'$ with its cached sizes…
nodes.title: Rank after deletion in an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an order-statistic tree over a linearly ordered key type whose cached subtree sizes are correct at every node and which is ordered. Then for every query $q$, the rank of $q$ computed by descending $T$ with cached left-subtree sizes equals the number of entries strictly smaller than $q$ in the inorder traversal of the binary tree obtained by erasing the caches of $T$.
nodes.title: Cached rank agrees with traversal rank

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an order-statistic tree over a linearly ordered type whose cached subtree sizes are correct and which satisfies the binary-search-tree ordering. If select at zero-based index $i$ in $T$ returns a key $k$, then the rank of $k$ in $T$ equals $i$.
nodes.title: Rank inverts select in an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: For a key $q$ of a linearly ordered type, the rank of $q$ in an order-statistic tree is computed by descending from the root. It is $0$ for the empty tree. At a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$, it is the rank of $q$ in $L$ if $q < k$; it is $s(L) + 1$ plus the rank of $q$ in $R$ if $k < q$; and it is $s(L)$ if $q = k$. Here $s(L)$ is the subtree size cached at the root of $L$, and $0$ if…
nodes.title: Rank in an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type and let $T$ be an order-statistic tree over $\alpha$ whose cached subtree sizes are correct. Let $k$ be a key and let $T'$ be the tree obtained from $T$ by deleting $k$. Then for every natural number $i$, selecting position $i$ in $T'$ by navigation with cached sizes returns the entry at zero-based position $i$ of the inorder traversal of $T'$ with its cached sizes removed,…
nodes.title: Selection after deletion in an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: For every order-statistic tree $T$ whose cached subtree sizes are correct and every natural number $i$, select at index $i$ in $T$ (descending with the cached sizes) returns the same result as taking the element at zero-based position $i$ of the inorder traversal of the binary tree obtained from $T$ by erasing the cached sizes; in particular both return nothing when that position does not exist.
nodes.title: Cached select agrees with inorder select

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, let $T$ be an order-statistic tree over $\alpha$ that is ordered and whose cached subtree sizes are correct, let $k$ be a key, and let $T'$ be the tree obtained from $T$ by deleting $k$. If $y$ is a key of $T'$, then selecting, with cached sizes, the position in $T'$ given by the cached rank of $y$ in $T'$ returns $y$.
nodes.title: Selecting the rank of a surviving key after deletion

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an order-statistic tree over a linearly ordered type whose cached subtree sizes are correct and which satisfies the binary-search-tree ordering. For every key $k$ in $T$, select in $T$ at the index equal to the rank of $k$ in $T$ returns $k$.
nodes.title: Select inverts rank in an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: For an order-statistic tree $T$ and a natural number $i$, select at index $i$ in $T$ is computed by descending from the root. It returns nothing for the empty tree. At a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$, it is select at index $i$ in $L$ if $i < s(L)$; it returns $k$ if $i = s(L)$; and it is select at index $i - s(L) - 1$ in $R$ if $i > s(L)$. Here $s(L)$ is the subtree size cached at the…
nodes.title: Select in an order-statistic tree

nodes.summary: An order-statistic tree with keys in a type $\alpha$ is a binary tree, possibly empty, each of whose nodes carries a key in $\alpha$ together with a natural number, meant as the cached number of nodes in the subtree rooted at that node. That these caches are correct is a separate condition.
nodes.title: Order-statistic tree
Computer Science

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
